Raza along with Ervine since then have fought back well but they need to keep going. Raza is very close to his fifty and Ervine would want to play a long innings again. Afghanistan on the other hand, will hope they can break this stand quickly after the break as wickets is the call for the hour for them. An interesting session awaits.

A really fine session of Test cricket! It began with Afghanistan running through the top order. Both Fareed Ahmad and Yamin Ahmadzai were at their best and got two each. They could have taken 5 had Raza not been dropped. That chance though is proving to be costly here.

Commentary.Commentary: All set for the action to begin!

They'll now be wanting to do well with the bat too! They will hope they can make most of the conditions which aren't that bad to bat. Afghanistan though will hope for their bowlers to deliver and get some early wickets. The first session is an important one. Stay tuned for it.

After five days of bat dominating in the first game, we had the bowlers finally coming to the party on Day 1 of the second. Also, it wasn't the visitors' bowlers who were the highlight but it was the hosts' bowlers who were absolutely brilliant. They justified their skipper's decision to bowl first and have bundled the hosts out for a very low score.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Zimbabwe have a good chance here to get well ahead in this game! They'll need their batters to apply the leaves and make use of a wicket which does not have a lot of demons in it. Afghanistan will hope their bowlers can do the job for them yet again. Do join us for Day 2 at 7.30 am GMT! Till then, goodbye and take care!

Zimbabwe Infact have done well throughout! There was long rain delay and after that, it was Zimbabwe who won the toss, elected to field and courtesy a combined bowling effort, bundled the visitors out for a low score and in reply too have played the little time they had to out well.

The light meter is out again and this time the umpires feel it's not good enough to continue and they go off! Just the three overs is what the Zimbabwe openers had to play and they have negotiated well.
